message.content: The sculpture that is often cited as the most iconic and widely recognized work of the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** (originally titled *Le Penseur*). Although the bronze version that most people see today was cast in 1902–1904, Rodin began working on the figure in 1880, and it was first exhibited in 1889 as part of his monumental project *The Gates of Hell*. The piece quickly became emblematic of modern sculpture, capturing the intellectual spirit of the era and influencing countless artists who followed. Its fame has endured into the present day, making it a quintessential symbol of 19th‑century sculpture.
